sources.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD) CVE API 2.0
sources.description: Official US government repository of CVE vulnerability records with CVSS scores, references and CPE configurations, exposed as a REST/JSON API.
sources.limitation: Rate-limited without an API key (5 requests per 30 seconds); a free API key only raises the limit. Content is subject to the NIST data source attribution policy.
sources.evidenceNote: Live JSON response for a single CVE returned with HTTP 200 and no authentication, demonstrating free keyless API access.

sources.name: abuse.ch URLhaus API
sources.description: Community-maintained database of malicious URLs and malware hosting endpoints, queryable via a REST API with bulk CSV exports.
sources.limitation: Community API is free under a fair-use policy and requires a free Auth-Key from auth.abuse.ch; commercial use requires a paid abuse.ch subscription.
sources.evidenceNote: Official API documentation stating the community API is available free of charge under the fair use policy with a free Auth-Key.

sources.name: MLB Stats API
sources.description: Live and historical Major League Baseball schedules, box scores, roster and stat endpoints operated by MLB Advanced Media, returning JSON.
sources.limitation: Unofficial public interface with no documented SLA and subject to change; all content is copyrighted by MLB Advanced Media, restricting redistribution.
sources.evidenceNote: Schedule endpoint returns HTTP 200 JSON with no registration or key, demonstrating free keyless access.

sources.name: iNaturalist API v1
sources.description: REST API over the community science biodiversity platform: observations, taxa, places and quality-graded species occurrence records worldwide.
sources.limitation: Anonymous requests are rate-limited and writes require a user token; observation data are shared under Creative Commons non-commercial licenses depending on the observer's choice.
sources.evidenceNote: Taxa search endpoint returned HTTP 200 JSON with no key, demonstrating free read access.

sources.name: Energy-Charts API (Fraunhofer ISE)
sources.description: Open API serving German and European electricity market time series from Fraunhofer ISE and BDEW: generation mix, prices, load and cross-border flows.
sources.limitation: Data cover primarily the German market; use is free for non-commercial purposes with attribution to Fraunhofer ISE/BDEW and reasonable-use traffic limits apply.
sources.evidenceNote: API root returns HTTP 200 identifying the public Energy-Charts API with no key requirement documented for read endpoints.

sources.name: Global Energy Monitor Tracker Databases
sources.description: Open-access crowdsourced datasets on global energy infrastructure: coal, gas, solar, wind, hydro and nuclear power plants, plus pipelines and heavy industry.
sources.limitation: Downloads are open access with attribution under the trackers' Creative Commons terms; snapshots are updated only per tracker release cycle and entries carry varying confidence flags.
sources.evidenceNote: Official download page describes the tracker data as open-access data available for public download without registration.

sources.name: legislation.gov.uk Legislation API
sources.description: The National Archives' API for consolidated UK legislation (Acts, Orders, measures) with permanent URIs and search, served in multiple machine-readable formats.
sources.limitation: Reuse is free under the Open Government Licence v3.0 with Crown copyright attribution; consolidated texts have documented editorial limitations and the API is governed by a fair use policy.
sources.evidenceNote: Official developer zone states the Legislation API is free to reuse and points to the Open Government Licence licensing terms.

sources.name: MBTA Developer API v3
sources.description: Official API of the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (Boston): real-time vehicle positions, predictions, routes, stops and alerts for subway, bus, rail and ferry.
sources.limitation: A free API key requires simple email registration; unauthenticated access is experimental and rate-limited, and per-key rate limits apply to heavy use.
sources.evidenceNote: Official MBTA developer portal: free API key sign-up for the v3 API.

sources.name: Transport for London Unified API
sources.description: Official TfL API covering routes, stops, arrivals, disruption and bike/scooter availability for London's bus, tube, rail, cycling and river services.
sources.limitation: Unregistered access is rate-limited and some premium endpoints (e.g. journey/planner data) require a free registered app key; data conditions follow TfL's open data terms.
sources.evidenceNote: Live endpoint returned HTTP 200 JSON with live bike-point data and no key, demonstrating free keyless access to core endpoints.

sources.name: Universal Dependencies
sources.description: Community project of cross-linguistically consistent treebank annotations: around 200 treebanks covering more than 150 languages in CoNLL-U format.
sources.limitation: Each treebank is released under its own Creative Commons license (mostly CC BY-SA) and must be cited per its own publication; annotation quality varies by language.
sources.evidenceNote: Official download page: all released treebanks are freely downloadable.

sources.name: swisstopo BGDI WMS (Federal Geoinformation)
sources.description: Swiss federal geospatial infrastructure operated by swisstopo: official maps, terrain, cadastral and land-cover layers served as OGC web services with GeoJSON feature output.
sources.limitation: Free to use with the mandatory source label '© swisstopo'; individual datasets can carry additional usage restrictions and reasonable-use traffic limits apply.
sources.evidenceNote: Official BGDI WMS GetCapabilities document advertises Fees: none and is published by the Federal Office of Topography swisstopo.

sources.name: NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69)
sources.description: Reference data for chemical species: thermochemistry, phase change, reaction kinetics and IR/MS spectra for tens of thousands of compounds.
sources.limitation: Open access under the NIST Standard Reference Data policy, but some entries carry original-literature copyright; NIST reserves the right to charge for some SRD products and citation of SRD 69 is requested.
sources.evidenceNote: NIST Standard Reference Data program page describes the SRDs, including the Chemistry WebBook, as freely available online reference data.

sources.name: Meteostat Weather & Climate Data
sources.description: Open platform with historical weather and climate time series for thousands of weather stations, available via JSON API, Python library and bulk CSV datasets.
sources.limitation: Free access requires crediting Meteostat and the originating national weather services; some station data remains subject to the providers' own license conditions.
sources.evidenceNote: Official developer portal states Meteostat provides free access to historical weather and climate data and documents the open JSON API and CSV datasets.

sources.name: OpenWeather Weather API
sources.description: Current weather, forecasts and historical data for any location worldwide via JSON APIs from the London-based OpenWeather (since 2012).
sources.limitation: The free subscription requires a free API key and caps calls (around 60 per minute / 1,000 per day) on a limited product set; granular historical and advanced products need paid plans.
sources.evidenceNote: Official pricing page offers a free subscription plan with self-service API key registration.

sources.name: Pew Research Center Datasets
sources.description: Microdata from Pew Research Center's public opinion and social trends surveys, downloadable as questionnaires and data files for secondary analysis.
sources.limitation: Downloads are free without registration but licensed for non-commercial research use with attribution to Pew Research Center; some series are country- or wave-specific.
sources.evidenceNote: Official datasets catalogue offers the survey data files for free download without an account.
